coverage_limit: A bounded 12-work primary-source map for continual learning, test-time learning, neural memory, and meta-learning. It is not a claim of exhaustive frontier coverage, an implementation recommendation, or evidence that any cited mechanism realizes HSWM. Each `date`/`year` is the source's first submission or publication date, not the date of the inspected revision. ArXiv works remain preprints here even where their metadata mentions a venue; peer-reviewed works are identified only by their proceedings/journal source. Two 2026 preprints were included only because their exact arXiv revision records were directly verified on 2026-09-07.
implementation_boundary: TTT, Titans, ATLAS, RMT, ARMT, and LRT alter or train a sequence-model backend. They cannot be inserted into the current token-native macro relation interpreter as a local feature. Any HSWM experiment using one requires an explicit backend/model replacement, source pin, capability boundary, matched comparator, and re-validation of the outcome-bound canonical learning loop.

works.title: Overcoming catastrophic forgetting in neural networks
works.mechanism: Elastic Weight Consolidation estimates which parameters mattered to earlier tasks and penalizes moving them while learning a new task, using a diagonal Fisher-information approximation.
works.hswm_bridge: SECONDARY_AI candidate: treat prior outcome-supported relation revisions as protected only under an explicit task or intervention scope; this suggests a stability control, not an HSWM owner or truth criterion.
works.limitation: A parameter-level, task-sequential approximation; it has no typed relation provenance, explicit revision lineage, or independent outcome-credit mechanism.
works.falsifier: Reject the stability-control bridge if a provenance-preserving replay or unconstrained revision achieves equal retained and new-task performance under equal capacity and compute.
works.verification_note: Primary PNAS record inspected; historical foundation retained deliberately, not presented as a current frontier result.

works.title: Recurrent Memory Transformer
works.mechanism: RMT adds trainable memory tokens to a segment-level recurrent Transformer, passing memory across segments so the model learns both memory operations and sequence processing.
works.hswm_bridge: SECONDARY_AI candidate: compare token-mediated bounded working configurations with HSWM sparse traversal; persistent memory tokens could only be a compiled read/write view of canonical atoms.
works.limitation: The recurrent token state is not a typed, independently owned relation graph and does not bind updates to external outcomes.
works.falsifier: Discard the bridge if bounded typed traversal cannot outperform or match memory-token recurrence on long-context tasks at equal context, state budget, and model.
works.verification_note: Exact inspected artifact: arXiv:2207.06881v2 (updated 2022-12-08); source date is its first submission, 2022-07-14.

works.title: Learning to (Learn at Test Time)
works.mechanism: The method uses an inner self-supervised learner for each instance and an outer loop that learns the inner task; special cases connect the learner to linear attention or kernel self-attention.
works.hswm_bridge: SECONDARY_AI candidate: evaluate an inner, episode-local relation proposal/update loop separately from a slower outcome-admitted canonical revision loop; using its neural inner learner would require backend replacement, not an interpreter patch.
works.limitation: Its learned self-supervision objective does not establish causal credit, safe admission, or persistence across a HSWM lineage.
works.falsifier: Reject the two-timescale bridge if episode-local proposals give no transfer or adaptation advantage over frozen retrieval at matched token and update budgets.
works.verification_note: Exact inspected artifact: arXiv:2310.13807v2 (updated 2024-01-07); source date is its first submission, 2023-10-20.

works.title: Learning to (Learn at Test Time): RNNs with Expressive Hidden States
works.mechanism: TTT layers make an RNN hidden state itself a learned linear model or MLP, then update it on test sequences with a self-supervised training step to retain longer context.
works.hswm_bridge: SECONDARY_AI candidate: a backend-replacement comparator for fast plasticity; it may be evaluated only by replacing/training the sequence model, while outcome-admitted graph revision stays explicitly outside its hidden state.
works.limitation: Updates derive from self-supervision on the current sequence; the paper does not provide typed claims, source provenance, rollback, or delayed external credit.
works.falsifier: The fast-plasticity bridge fails if a frozen context/RAG baseline equals the changed-next-action effect after matching context and compute.
works.verification_note: Exact inspected artifact: arXiv:2407.04620v4 (updated 2025-08-31); source date is its first submission, 2024-07-05.

works.title: Rehearsal-Free Modular and Compositional Continual Learning for Language Models
works.mechanism: MoCL continually adds language-model modules and composes new modules with prior ones, aiming to avoid rehearsal while preserving transfer across tasks.
works.hswm_bridge: SECONDARY_AI candidate: an empirical comparator for whether HSWM relation composition and provenance-preserving revisions give benefit beyond modular parameter isolation.
works.limitation: Modules and task-based composition are not schema-relative canonical atoms, and the work does not identify causal credit for individual relations.
works.falsifier: Reject a compositional-graph advantage if MoCL or another module-isolation baseline matches HSWM forward transfer and retention under equal total parameters and data access.
works.verification_note: Exact inspected artifact: arXiv:2404.00790v1; source date is its first submission, 2024-03-31.

works.title: Associative Recurrent Memory Transformer
works.mechanism: ARMT combines local self-attention with segment-level recurrence to store task-specific information over long context, reporting associative-retrieval and BABILong results.
works.hswm_bridge: SECONDARY_AI candidate: a long-context associative-memory baseline for checking whether typed relation selection improves decisions rather than merely retaining more sequence information.
works.limitation: It is a sequence-memory architecture without canonical relation identity, source lineage, or an outcome-bound update rule.
works.falsifier: The bridge fails if ARMT matches any HSWM retrieval and next-action advantage when given identical observations and memory capacity.
works.verification_note: Exact inspected artifact: arXiv:2407.04841v2 (updated 2025-02-13); source date is its first submission, 2024-07-05.

works.title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time
works.mechanism: Titans pairs attention over current context with a neural long-term memory module that learns to memorize historical context at test time, with three architectural variants.
works.hswm_bridge: SECONDARY_AI candidate: a backend-replacement fast-memory baseline; its surprise-driven neural updates can inform a separately implemented proposal-ranking experiment but cannot be inserted into the interpreter or promote a relation without provenance and independent outcome credit.
works.limitation: Neural-memory parameters compress source and relation detail; the paper does not supply typed n-ary relations, revision ownership, rollback, or independent outcome admission.
works.falsifier: The bridge fails if frozen retrieval or Titans explains the same fresh-probe action change as outcome-admitted canonical relation revision under matched compute.
works.verification_note: Exact inspected artifact: arXiv:2501.00663v1; source date is its first submission, 2024-12-31. Repository already cites this work as an architectural neighbour.

works.title: ATLAS: Learning to Optimally Memorize the Context at Test Time
works.mechanism: ATLAS optimizes a high-capacity long-term memory using current and past tokens rather than only the latest input, yielding a DeepTransformer family for long-context tasks.
works.hswm_bridge: SECONDARY_AI candidate: a backend-replacement past-token-memory comparator. A HSWM study must compare it with a bounded relation-learning candidate generator and require the latter to prove changed observation/action under an explicit outcome contract.
works.limitation: Its fixed-size neural memory has no explicit typed hypergraph, canonical lifecycle, or independently auditable causal admission.
works.falsifier: Reject the bridge if ATLAS matches HSWM relation-learning gains on held-out interventions with identical base model, observations, and compute.
works.verification_note: Exact inspected artifact: arXiv:2505.23735v1; source date is its first submission, 2025-05-29.

works.title: ZeroFlow: Overcoming Catastrophic Forgetting is Easier than You Think
works.mechanism: ZeroFlow presents forward-pass-based optimization principles for reducing forgetting, managing task conflicts, and lowering memory demands in continual learning.
works.hswm_bridge: SECONDARY_AI candidate: a low-cost comparator for relation-update gating, testing whether forward-only signals can screen proposals before costly outcome evaluation.
works.limitation: The method targets conventional continual-learning retention; it does not provide a semantics for relation claims, provenance, intervention, or external causal credit.
works.falsifier: Do not adopt forward-only screening if it misses outcome-valid relation revisions or has no lower-cost/equal-quality advantage against direct outcome evaluation.
works.verification_note: Primary ICML 2025 PMLR record and abstract directly inspected.

works.title: Nested Learning: The Illusion of Deep Learning Architectures
works.mechanism: Nested Learning casts a model as nested, multilevel, or parallel optimization problems with context flows; it proposes expressive optimizers, a self-modifying sequence model, and a continuum-memory formulation.
works.hswm_bridge: SECONDARY_AI candidate: formalize candidate relation induction, outcome evaluation, and canonical admission as separate nested optimization/control levels with non-interchangeable evidence contracts.
works.limitation: The paper's optimization-level account neither supplies HSWM's schema-relative owner/provenance requirements nor demonstrates outcome-bound causal learning in a typed hypergraph.
works.falsifier: The bridge fails if adding its proposed levels does not improve pre-registered transfer, retention, and intervention-sensitive action versus a simpler single-level learner at matched resources.
works.verification_note: Exact inspected artifact: arXiv:2512.24695v1; source date is its first submission, 2025-12-31. Its arXiv metadata says a version was published at NeurIPS 2025, but that venue artifact was not inspected here.

works.title: Latent Recurrent Transformer: Architecture Exploration, Training Strategies, and Scaling Behavior
works.mechanism: LRT reuses a high-level hidden state from the preceding token as cross-layer recurrent memory and trains it with interleaved parallel refinement rather than fully sequential unrolling.
works.hswm_bridge: SECONDARY_AI candidate: a backend-replacement comparator for low-overhead latent recurrence against explicit relation-state reads, separating context-efficiency measurements from claims of durable learning.
works.limitation: A recurrent latent state is opaque to typed relation inspection and carries no source, revision, rollback, or outcome-credit contract.
works.falsifier: Treat it as an insufficient bridge if latent recurrence produces the same action performance as relation reads and intervention on relation state adds no effect at matched context budget.
works.verification_note: Exact inspected artifact: arXiv:2605.26797v2 (updated 2026-09-01); source date is its first submission, 2026-05-26. Abstract only; no implementation or efficacy claim is imported.

works.title: Extending LLM Context via Associative Recurrent Memory
works.mechanism: The work studies ARMT for LLM context extension, combining continued pre-training, synthetic long-context data, curriculum learning, and selective associative-memory layers.
works.hswm_bridge: SECONDARY_AI candidate: a backend-replacement external baseline for long-context state persistence; use it to test whether HSWM relation lineage adds intervention-sensitive learning rather than merely context extension.
works.limitation: It reports architecture/training results, not a typed causal-learning graph or a canonical relation-admission pathway.
works.falsifier: The bridge fails if ARMT's recurrent memory equals HSWM on held-out changed-relation action tests and no lineage or rollback intervention yields measurable additional benefit.
works.verification_note: Exact inspected artifact: arXiv:2607.11614v1; source date is its first submission, 2026-07-13. Abstract only; no peer-review status inferred.
